proposals.before: He became prefect of Ninghua Army and Fengzhou, transferred to Xida River superintendent; when he met Tong Guan he did not bow, and Guan resented this.
proposals.after: He became prefect of Ninghua Army and Fengzhou, transferred to Xida River superintendent; when he met Tong Guan he did not bow, and Tong resented this.
proposals.reason: The resentful 貫 is Tong Guan, not He Guan; the literal English Guan is ambiguous and reverses the referent.

proposals.before: The pacification commissioner, jealous of him, impeached him for claiming rewards before the cloud-board fortifications were finished. Guan was stripped of his latest promotion, demoted again in rank, and removed from office.
proposals.after: The pacification commissioner, jealous of him, impeached him, saying the rammed-earth fortifications were not yet finished and he had claimed the reward. Guan was stripped of his latest promotion, demoted again in rank, and removed from office.
proposals.reason: 雲 here introduces the charge (saying that); 板築 is rammed-earth construction, not cloud-board fortifications.

proposals.before: The pacification commissioner envied him, impeached that cloud boards and fortifications were not finished yet he claimed reward, stripped the office to which he had been promoted, demoted him in rank again, and dismissed him.
proposals.after: The pacification commissioner envied him, impeached him alleging that the rammed-earth fortifications were not finished yet he had claimed the reward, stripped the office to which he had been promoted, demoted him in rank again, and dismissed him.
proposals.reason: Same 雲板築 misreading as cloud boards rather than an allegation about rammed-earth work.

proposals.before: Before long he became prefect of Minzhou, led Miaochuan water to irrigate a thousand qing of dry land; Qinghai people called it the Broad Benefit Canal.
proposals.after: Before long he became prefect of Minzhou, led Miaochuan water to irrigate a thousand qing of dry land; the people of Huang called it the Broad Benefit Canal.
proposals.reason: 湟人 are people of Huang, not anachronistic Qinghai.

proposals.before: When Tong Guan campaigned in the west, Guan seized Gulong horses of antiquity for the Wujun Army, was made defense commissioner of Jizhou, and was reassigned as prefect of Lanzhou.
proposals.after: When Tong Guan campaigned in the west, Guan took Gugulong and the Majinwu Army, was made defense commissioner of Jizhou, and was reassigned as prefect of Lanzhou.
proposals.reason: 古骨龍 and 馬進武軍 are place/army names, not ancient Gulong horses advancing the Wujun Army.

proposals.before: When Tong Guan campaigned on the western border, Guan took ancient Gulong horses to advance the Wujun Army, was added Jizhou defense commissioner, and changed to Lanzhou prefect.
proposals.after: When Tong Guan campaigned on the western border, Guan took Gugulong and the Majinwu Army, was added Jizhou defense commissioner, and changed to Lanzhou prefect.
proposals.reason: Same mis-segmentation of 古骨龍馬進武軍.

proposals.before: Aguda bypassed Jingzhou and besieged Jizhou.
proposals.after: Kuilibu bypassed Jingzhou and besieged Jizhou.
proposals.reason: 夔離不 is not Aguda (阿骨打); the English substitutes the wrong Jin figure.

proposals.before: Aguda did not take Jingzhou but besieged Jizhou.
proposals.after: Kuilibu did not take Jingzhou but besieged Jizhou.
proposals.reason: Same wrong identification of 夔離不 as Aguda; 取 here is to take/capture Jingzhou.

proposals.before: Guan took responsibility for the military situation, quickly recovered Jing city, and lifted the siege of Ji.
proposals.after: Tong Guan palmed the military situation off on him; he quickly recovered Jing city and lifted the siege of Ji.
proposals.reason: 貫諉以兵事 means Tong Guan shifted/shirked the fighting onto He Guan, not that He Guan took responsibility.

proposals.before: Prince Yun Cai came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said, "The succession is already settled—under whose orders does Your Highness come?"
proposals.after: Kai, Prince of Yun, came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said, "The succession is already settled—under whose orders does Your Highness come?"
proposals.reason: 鄆王楷 is Kai, Prince of Yun; Cai misreads 楷.

proposals.before: The Prince of Yun, Cai, came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said: "The great matter is already settled; from whom does Your Highness receive orders to come?"
proposals.after: The Prince of Yun, Kai, came to the gate wishing to enter. Guan said: "The great matter is already settled; from whom does Your Highness receive orders to come?"
proposals.reason: Same 楷/Cai error in the literal English.

proposals.before: Wang Fu had stepped down as Grand Chancellor but still headed the Imperial Offerings Office. He was then pursuing the Yan-Yun campaign and set up a frontier pacification office within the Secretariat that he alone controlled; the other chief ministers were excluded.
proposals.after: Wang Fu, as Grand Chancellor, also headed the Imperial Offerings Office. He was then pursuing the Yan-Yun campaign and set up a frontier pacification office within the Secretariat that he alone controlled; the other chief ministers were excluded.
proposals.reason: Chinese 王黼乙太宰領應奉司 is 以太宰: he headed the office as Grand Chancellor, not after stepping down.

proposals.before: Wang Fu, having resigned as Grand Chancellor, still headed the Imperial Offerings Office; he was also then engaged in Yan-Yun affairs and established a frontier pacification office within the Secretariat that he alone controlled; other chief ministers could not participate.
proposals.after: Wang Fu, as Grand Chancellor, headed the Imperial Offerings Office; he was also then engaged in Yan-Yun affairs and established a frontier pacification office within the Secretariat that he alone controlled; other chief ministers could not participate.
proposals.reason: The source does not say he had resigned; 乙太宰 is 以太宰, holding the chancellorship while leading the offerings office.

proposals.before: His father Xiankhe rose to prefect of Yingzhou and administrator of Luzhou.
proposals.after: His father Xianke rose to prefect of Yingzhou and administrator of Luzhou.
proposals.reason: 獻可 is Xianke; Xiankhe is a corrupted romanization.

proposals.before: His father Xiankhe served to Yingzhou prefect and Luzhou prefect.
proposals.after: His father Xianke served to Yingzhou prefect and Luzhou prefect.
proposals.reason: 獻可 is Xianke; the inserted h is not in the name.

proposals.before: In Jingkang 1 he was sent as supervising secretary to Wanyan Zonghan's camp to negotiate ceding the three prefectures in exchange for peace.
proposals.after: In Jingkang 1 he was sent as supervising secretary to Wolibu's camp to negotiate ceding the three prefectures in exchange for peace.
proposals.reason: 斡離不 is Wolibu (Wanyan Zongwang), not Wanyan Zonghan (黏罕).

proposals.before: In the first year of Jingkang he was sent as supervising secretary to Wanyan Zonghan's army to negotiate ceding the three prefectures for peace.
proposals.after: In the first year of Jingkang he was sent as supervising secretary to Wolibu's army to negotiate ceding the three prefectures for peace.
proposals.reason: 斡離不 is Wolibu, not Wanyan Zonghan.

proposals.before: On his return he reported Zonghan's message: Aguda had obtained a wax-sealed letter from the court to Yelü Yu and insisted that the Song could not be trusted, intending to break the peace treaty.
proposals.after: On his return he reported Wolibu's message: Nianhan had obtained a wax-sealed letter from the court to Yelü Yudu and insisted that the Song could not be trusted, intending to break the peace treaty.
proposals.reason: 斡離不 is Wolibu; 黏罕 is Nianhan, not Aguda; 餘睹 is Yelü Yudu.

proposals.before: On his return he relayed Zonghan's meaning, saying that Wanyan Aguda had obtained from the court a wax-sealed letter to Yelü Yu, and firmly declared China untrustworthy, wishing to break the peace treaty.
proposals.after: On his return he relayed Wolibu's meaning, saying that Nianhan had obtained from the court a wax-sealed letter to Yelü Yudu, and firmly declared the Central States untrustworthy, wishing to break the peace treaty.
proposals.reason: The names 斡離不 and 黏罕 are misidentified in the English; Aguda is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: The emperor feared he would be detained. Yun said: "Once peace is concluded there can be no reason to detain the prince; I dare guarantee this with the lives of a hundred in my household."
proposals.after: The emperor feared the prince would be detained. Yun said: "Once peace is concluded there can be no reason to detain the prince; I dare guarantee this with the lives of a hundred in my household."
proposals.reason: The pronoun in 帝慮為所留 refers to the Prince of Kang, not Yun; the idiomatic already names the prince, but the literal leaves a false referent.

proposals.before: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the state he ordered Shiji and Li Xijing to serve together in the Hanlin Academy; both claimed illness and would not rise, and died of grief at age fifty-four.
proposals.after: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the state he ordered Shiji and Li Xijing to serve together in the Hanlin Academy; both claimed illness and would not rise, and Shiji died of grief at age fifty-four.
proposals.reason: The age fifty-four and death from grief belong to Tan Shiji's biography, not to both men jointly; the literal makes both die at fifty-four.

proposals.before: Zhili read it once and knew it was false; he wished to report it but his superiors hesitated and dared not; he alone memorialized that it was a border fraud.
proposals.after: Zhili read it once and knew it was false; he wished to report it but his superiors hesitated and dared not; he alone memorialized that it was a fraud.
proposals.reason: 界詐 means the claim was fraudulent; 界 is not the border. The idiomatic line already says false claim.

proposals.before: He had long been on good terms with Wang Fu, who once gave a banquet at Zhili's residence and displayed the splendor of his gardens, ponds, and courtesans with evident pride.
proposals.after: He had long been on good terms with Wang Fu, who once gave a banquet at his own residence and displayed the splendor of his gardens, ponds, and courtesans with evident pride.
proposals.reason: 黼嘗置酒其第 is Wang Fu hosting at his own mansion and showing off his gardens and attendants, not a banquet at Mei Zhili's house.

proposals.before: When the Jin besieged the capital Zhili urged the emperor to take the field in person and asked that the Retired Emperor, the empress, and the crown prince all withdraw to safety—those in power blocked the plan.
proposals.after: When the Jin besieged the capital Zhili urged the emperor to take the field in person and asked that the Retired Emperor and Empress, the empress, and the crown prince all withdraw to safety—those in power blocked the plan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太上帝后、皇后、太子 lists retired emperor and retired empress plus the reigning empress and crown prince; the idiomatic line collapses 太上帝后.

proposals.before: Li did not follow this.
proposals.after: He Li would not follow this.
proposals.reason: Literal English reduces 栗 to the given name Li and loses the surname 何 established in the previous sentence.

proposals.before: Chen Zhizhi, vice minister of Rites, who died at the same time, has no surviving biography; An Fu, Secretariat drafter, is treated in his father's biography of An Tao.
proposals.after: Chen Zhizhi, vice minister of Rites, who died at the same time, has no surviving biography; An Fu, supervising secretary, is treated in his father's biography of An Tao.
proposals.reason: 給事中 was already rendered supervising secretary in this chapter; Secretariat drafter is 中書舍人.

proposals.before: Chen Zhizhi, vice minister of Rites, who died at the same time, has lost his biography; An Fu, Secretariat drafter, is treated in his father's biography of An Tao.
proposals.after: Chen Zhizhi, vice minister of Rites, who died at the same time, has lost his biography; An Fu, supervising secretary, is treated in his father's biography of An Tao.
proposals.reason: Same office error as the idiomatic line: 給事中 is not Secretariat drafter.

proposals.before: His family for generations were military men; bold and brave, he followed several western campaigns, won battle merit, and rose through offices to Tongzhou observation commissioner, commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard, and overall commander of the Fuyan route.
proposals.after: His family for generations were military men; bold and brave, he followed several western campaigns, won battle merit, and rose through offices to Xiangzhou observation commissioner, commander of the Dragon and Divine Guard, and overall commander of the Fuyan route.
proposals.reason: Chinese 相州 is Xiangzhou; Tongzhou is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: Yaoshi said, "Gan's troops number no more than ten thousand. He is exerting all his strength to resist us, so Yan Mountain must be empty. Give me five thousand picked troops to march by forced stages and seize it, with your son the Third General Jian leading the follow-up force."
proposals.after: Yaoshi said, "Gan's troops number no more than ten thousand. He is exerting all his strength to resist us, so Yan Mountain must be empty. Give me five thousand picked troops to march by forced stages and seize it, with your son the Third General selecting a force as the follow-up."
proposals.reason: 簡師 means to select troops, not a personal name Jian; the next sentence identifies the Third General as Guangshi.

proposals.before: Huizong took the point and wished to cut excess and distance his close attendants, but eunuchs like Yang Kai were building palaces on a grand scale and feared they would lose their freedom. They slandered the household steward Yang Feng, claiming he would help the crown prince seize power irregularly.
proposals.after: Huizong took the point and wished to cut excess and distance his close attendants, but eunuchs like Yang Jian were building palaces on a grand scale and feared they would lose their freedom. They slandered the household steward Yang Feng, claiming he would help the crown prince seize power irregularly.
proposals.reason: 楊戩 is Yang Jian (Jiǎn), not Yang Kai.

proposals.before: The court held that Yanqing had lost the army and the law could not go unenforced. He was demoted to commandant of the Commandant's Office and settled at Yunzhou.
proposals.after: The court held that Yanqing had lost the army and the law could not go unenforced. He was demoted to commandant of the Commandant's Office and settled at Junzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 筠州 is Junzhou; Yunzhou would write 雲州, so the English place-name is a mistranslation.

proposals.before: The court debated that Yanqing had lost the army and the law could not go unenforced; he was demoted to commandant of the Commandant's Office and settled at Yunzhou.
proposals.after: The court debated that Yanqing had lost the army and the law could not go unenforced; he was demoted to commandant of the Commandant's Office and settled at Junzhou.
proposals.reason: Chinese 筠州 is Junzhou; Yunzhou would write 雲州, so the English place-name is a mistranslation.

decisions.reason: 貫憾焉 resumes 童貫; the biography’s English Guan otherwise names 何灌, so “Guan resented this” assigns the resentment to the wrong man.
劾雲 introduces the charge (云/雲 “saying that”); 板築 is rammed-earth work, not “cloud-board fortifications.”
The literal likewise treats 雲板築 as “cloud boards”; the impeachment alleges unfinished rammed-earth construction and a false reward claim.
湟人 are the people of Huang; Qinghai is an anachronistic geographic gloss not in the Chinese.
灌取古骨龍馬進武軍 names the place 古骨龍 and the 馬進武軍, not ancient Gulong horses or a Wujun Army.
The same mis-segmentation of 古骨龍馬進武軍 must be corrected in the literal line.

decisions.after: Kuilibu took Jingzhou and besieged Jizhou.
decisions.reason: 夔離不 is not Aguda, but the proposed line still renders 取景州 as “bypassed.” s0036 復景城 shows Jing had been taken.

decisions.after: Kuilibu took Jingzhou and besieged Jizhou.
decisions.reason: The original parsed the 不 of 夔離不 as negation (“did not take”); the proposal keeps that false 不取 while only fixing the name. 取景州 is capture.
貫 is 童貫 and 諉以兵事 is shifting the fighting onto He Guan, not He Guan “taking responsibility.”
鄆王楷 is Kai, Prince of Yun; Cai is a misreading of 楷.
The literal likewise misreads 楷 as Cai.
乙太宰 is 以太宰: he led the Offerings Office as Grand Chancellor. s0076 非宰相所當預 confirms he still was chief minister; “stepped down” is invented.
The source does not say he had resigned; 以太宰領應奉司 is concurrent tenure.
獻可 is Xianke; the inserted h in Xiankhe is not in the name.
The literal needs the same correction of 獻可 to Xianke.
斡離不 is Wolibu (Wanyan Zongwang). Wanyan Zonghan is 黏罕, named only in the next sentence.
The literal likewise misidentifies 斡離不 as Wanyan Zonghan.
斡離不之意 is Wolibu’s message; 黏罕 is Nianhan, not Aguda; 餘睹 is Yelü Yudu.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 傳道斡離不之意，以為黏罕得朝廷所與餘睹蠟書

decisions.reason: Aguda is not in the Chinese; the names are Wolibu, Nianhan, and Yelü Yudu. Rendering 中國 as “the Central States” is a fair literal choice.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 斡離不之意，以為黏罕得朝廷所與餘睹蠟書

decisions.reason: 帝慮為所留 follows the plan to send the Prince of Kang; the one feared detained is the prince, not Yun.
皆稱疾臥不起 covers both men; 以憂卒，年五十四 is the biography’s death notice for Tan Shiji alone. Li Xijing’s death at fifty-three is already recorded earlier.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 皆稱疾臥不起，以憂卒，年五十四

decisions.reason: The tea-certificate case is fraud; 界詐也 does not mean a border offense. The idiomatic line already has “false claim.”
黼嘗置酒其第: 其第 is Wang Fu’s own mansion, whose gardens and attendants he displays; Zhili’s rebuke in s0175–s0176 treats Fu as the proud host.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 黼嘗置酒其第，誇示園池妓妾之盛

decisions.after: When the Jin besieged the capital Zhili urged the emperor to take the field in person and asked that the Retired Emperor and Retired Empress, the empress, and the crown prince all withdraw to safety—those in power blocked the plan.
decisions.reason: 太上帝后 is the retired emperor and retired empress, then 皇后 and 太子. The proposal restores the missing person but “Retired Emperor and Empress, the empress” is awkward.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 請太上帝后、皇后、太子皆出避

decisions.reason: 栗 resumes 何栗 from the previous sentence; bare English Li reads as the surname 李.
給事中 is supervising secretary in this chapter; Secretariat drafter is 中書舍人.
The literal has the same office error for 給事中.
相州 is Xiangzhou; Tongzhou would be 同州, already used elsewhere in the chapter for a different prefecture.
簡師為後繼 is to select a force as the follow-up, not a personal name Jian. s0261 identifies the Third General as Guangshi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 令公之子三將軍簡師為後繼

decisions.reason: 楊戩 is Yang Jian (Jiǎn); Kai is a wrong reading of 戩.
筠州 is Yunzhou in pinyin (yún). Junzhou is the usual English for a different prefecture, 均州. Homophony with 雲州 does not make Yunzhou a mistranslation of 筠.
The literal Yunzhou likewise matches 筠州; replacing it with Junzhou would invite confusion with 均州.

claimRetractions.reason: Revised r0007 shows Aguda is not in 夔離不 and is not an alias of this Jin commander.
The unit only has 夔離不 taking Jingzhou and besieging Jizhou. Warlord is not in the Chinese and was inferred from the false Aguda identification.

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0007 restores 夔離不 as Kuilibu; English Aguda was produced only by the mistranslation.
取景州 is capture, confirmed by 復景城 in s0036; “bypassed” existed only in the bad English.
Accepted r0010 shows Prince Yun Cai was a misreading of 楷; the personal name is Kai, Prince of Yun.
Accepted r0014 restores Xianke for 獻可; Xiankhe was only a corrupt romanization.
Accepted r0016 shows Wanyan Zonghan was substituted for 斡離不; the named commander is Wolibu.
Accepted r0018 restores Wolibu for 斡離不 in s0102; Zonghan names 黏罕, a different man.
黏罕 is Nianhan; Aguda (阿骨打) is not in this unit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以為黏罕得朝廷所與餘睹蠟書

claimRevisions.reason: 餘睹 is Yelü Yudu; Yu drops 睹.
太上帝后 names the retired emperor and retired empress together; Huizong’s title in the phrase is 太上, not the whole compound.

urged personal campaign and evacuation of the retired emperor and retired empress, the empress, and the crown prince

claimRevisions.reason: The evacuation list in 太上帝后、皇后、太子 includes the retired empress, omitted from the extracted action.
